content:
Kylie Kelce has publicly apologised for the way she referred to the Princess of Wales on a recent episode of her podcast Not Gonna Lie.

The former hockey player invited the royal onto her podcast after Prince William recently appeared on New Heights, hosted by Kelce's husband and his brother-in-law.

"Princess Catherine, Duchess of Cambridge, if you want to come up and talk hockey, talk parenting, we would love to have you," Kelce said. She added: "We have a few things in common."

Kate Middleton became the Duchess of Cambridge, Catherine, after marrying Prince William in April 2011.

Following the death of Queen Elizabeth II, her title is now Princess of Wales, Catherine. King Charles, the former Prince of Wales, granted the Prince and Princess of Wales titles to his son and daughter-in-law after ascending to the throne. HuffPost will continue to refer to her as Kate Middleton on first reference because that is how she is most easily searched for and referenced online.

Kelce later corrected her reference to Catherine on the October 1 episode of her podcast.

"I love learning, so I didn't know that calling Princess Catherine 'Princess Kate' would be offensive to people. I didn't know that before, now I do. I'll do better going forward. I apologise for that mistake, and I want to refer to people in the most respectful way, the way they want to be respected," the podcast host said.

"Princess Catherine is the correct way — or Princess of Wales. I apologise, and I'll do better starting right now."

Kelce also referenced a message someone left her that read: "Princess Catherine is too elegant and beautiful to be subjected to your foul language... You need to check yourself."

The mother of four did not push back.

"First of all, you're right, I would love to talk to the Princess of Wales. OK? For so many reasons. She is an incredible woman, she has little kids, she played hockey, she fought cancer. There are so many things I want to talk to her about," she said with a laugh.

"Do I think she has time to come on this podcast? No, I don't," she said, though Kelce said she would absolutely not swear in front of the royal if she did appear.

"You know what, I love to swear. I love it so much. You all know I love to swear," she said. "But at the end of the day, I do read the room and at the very least be respectful to the person I'm sitting across from."

It's possible the royal could appear via Zoom, as Catherine previously appeared on Giovanna Fletcher's podcast Happy Mum, Happy Baby in February 2020.
